questions.question: In the state of ______, the general direction of the Himalayas is from southwest to northeast.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh.**__

__
 
• Himalayas in the Darjiling and Sikkim regions lie in an east west direction, while in** Arunachal Pradesh** they are from southwest to the northwest direction. 
 
• Dihang River/Siang River is the name given to Brahmaputra River in Arunachal Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The Himalayas are classified into different divisions by Rivers flowing between them.

 
 

 
 
Punjab/Kashmir Himalayas

 
 
 
The part of the Himalayas that lies between the Indus River and Satluj River.

 
 
 

 
 
Kumaon Himalayas

 
 
 
The part of the Himalayas that lies between Satluj River and Kali River.

 
 
 

 
 
Nepal Himalayas

 
 
 
The part of the Himalayas that lies between the Kali River and Teesta River.

 
 
 

 
 
Assam Himalayas

 
 
 
The part of the Himalayas that lies between the Teesta River and Dihang River.

 
 
 

 
 
Purvanchal / Eastern Himalayas

 
 
 
The part of the Himalayas that lies beyond Dihang River valley.

 
Here the Himalayas bend sharply towards the south and spread along Indo-Myanmar Border.

questions.question: Which of the following is a part of the central processing unit of a computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Memory registers.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A central processing unit (CPU), also called a central processor, main processor or just processor.
 
• It is the electronic circuitry that executes instructions comprising a computer program.
 
• The CPU performs basic arithmetic, logic, controlling, and input/output (I/O) operations specified by the instructions in the program.
 
• This contrasts with external components such as main memory and I/O circuitry, and specialized processors such as graphics processing units.
 
• Principal components of a CPU include:** ****Control Unit, Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), Memory Registers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Control Unit:

 
• A control unit that orchestrates the fetching (from memory) and execution of instructions by directing the coordinated operations of the ALU, registers and other components.
 
• The control unit (CU) is a component of a computer's central processing unit (CPU) that directs the operation of the processor.
 
• It tells the computer's memory, arithmetic logic unit and input and output devices how to respond to the instructions that have been sent to the processor.

ALU:

 
• The arithmetic logic unit (ALU) performs arithmetic and logic operations.
 
• In computing, an arithmetic logic unit is a combination digital circuit that performs arithmetic and bitwise operations on integer binary numbers. This is in contrast to a floating-point unit, which operates on floating-point numbers.

Registers:

 
• Processor registers that supply operands to the ALU and store the results of ALU operations.
 
• A processor register is a quickly accessible location available to a computer's processor.
 
• Registers usually consist of a small amount of fast storage, although some registers have specific hardware functions, and maybe read-only or write-only.

Thus the Central Processing Unit (CPU) in a computer consists of Control unit, arithmetic logic unit, and memory registers.

questions.question: What is the total charge of an electric dipole?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• An electric dipole is pair of equal and opposite charges separated by a distance of 2a, the midpoint of locations -q and + q is called the centre of the dipole.
 
• The total charge of an electric dipole is **zero.**
 
• Electric dipole moment is the product of the magnitude of one charge multiplied by the distance of separation between the charge and is given by

⇒ P = 2a × q

Where P = dipole moment, 2a = Distance between the charge, and q = Charge

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Government of India set up the Monetary Policy Committee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2016.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 2016 the Government of India set up the Monetary Policy Committee.**
 
• The Central Government in September 2016 constituted the MPC as under:-
 
 
• **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India - Chairperson, ex officio.**
 
• Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, in charge of Monetary Policy - Member, ex officio.
 
• One officer of the Reserve Bank of In be nominated by the Central Board - Member, ex officio; Shri Chetan Ghate, Professor, Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) – Member;
 
• Professor Pami Dua, Director, Delhi School of Economics - Member, and Dr Ravindra H. Dholakia, Professor, Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad - Member.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monetary Policy:**

 
 
• It refers to the management of money supply for achieving macroeconomic objectives such as controlling inflation, consumption, growth, and liquidity.
 
• In India, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is vested with the responsibility of conducting monetary policy. This responsibility is explicitly mandated under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The primary objective of monetary policy is to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
 
• In May 2016, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, 1934 was amended and provides a basis for the implementation of a flexible inflation targeting framework.
 
• Now the inflation target is set by GOI in consultation with RBI once every five years.
 
• Currently, the inflation rate target is 4 per cent, with a band of +/- 2 per cent It means if the inflation rate is below 2 then GOI and RBI will increase the inflation and if it is above 6 then they will try to reduce the inflation Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act, 1934 also provides for an empowered six-member monetary policy committee (MPC) to be constituted by the Central Government.

questions.question: What does LED stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Light Emitting Diode.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The LED (light-emitting diode) **is a** PN junction device **that emits light when a current passes through it in the forward direction, i.e. when LED is forward biased, it emits light.
 
• In an LED, this energy lies in the visible region of electromagnetic radiation, and the photon released is perceived as light.
 
• An LED in this way converts electrical energy into light energy.
 
• In reverse biased mode, it works like a normal diode and does not emit light.
 
• It is an optical semiconductor device that emits light when voltage is applied means it converts electrical energy into light energy.
 
• **When Light Emitting Diode (LED) is forward biased, the free electrons from the n-side and the holes from the p-side are pushed towards the junction.**
 
• Light-emitting diodes emit either visible light or invisible infrared light when forward biased.
 
• The LEDs which emit invisible infrared light are used for remote controls.
 
• **LEDs that can emit red, yellow, orange, green, and blue light are available for commercial use.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: What is India’s rank according to the ‘Human Development report 2020’ released by the United Nations Development Programme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__131.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India ranked at 131st position out of 189 countries in the Human Development Index 2020.**
 
• This report was published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• HDI emphasizes that people and their capabilities should be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of a country, not economic growth alone.
 
• **It is a composite index that measures average achievement in three basic dimensions of human development- a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living.**
 
• The 2020 Report has introduced planetary pressures-adjust Development Index (HDI) by a country per capita carbon dioxide emissions and material footprint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structure of the 2020 Human Development Report:**

 
 
• Renewing human development for the Anthropocene.
 
• Mechanisms of change to catalyze action.
 
• Exploring new metrics.
 
 
 
• **Human Development Index is the measure of a nation's health, education, and standards of living.**
 
• The life expectancy of Indians at** birth in 2019 was 69.7 years while Bangladesh has a life expectancy of 72.6 years and Pakistan 67.3 years.**
 
• The HDI was created to emphasize that people and their capabilities should be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of a country, not economic growth alone.
 
• The HDI can also be used to question national policy choices, asking how two countries with the same level of GNI per capita can end up with different human development outcomes.
 
• These contrasts can stimulate debate about government policy priorities.
 
• **The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary measure of average achievement in key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, being knowledgeable and having a decent standard of living.**

questions.question: Which of the following does the Special Marriage Act 1954 NOT support?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Strict endogamy.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The Special Marriage Act, 1954 is an Act of the Parliament of India with provision for civil marriage (registered marriage) for people of India and all Indian nationals in foreign countries, irrespective of the religion or faith followed by either party.
 
• Special marriage acts support Communal harmony, Interfaith marriage, Inter-caste marriage.
 
 
• The Special Marriage Act, of 1954 replaced the old Act III, 1872.
 
• The new enactment had three major objectives:
 
 
• To provide a special form of marriage in certain cases,
 
• To provide for the registration of certain marriages and,
 
• To provide for divorce
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Endogamy refers to marriage within a unit (like kin, group, caste). It is also called in-marriage.
 
• These type of marriages takes place within a particular social group such as caste, clan, tribe, gotra, etc.
 
• Exogamy is referred to as marriage to an outside group.
 
• Polygyny means where a man has multiple simultaneous wives.
 
• Polyandry means a woman has multiple simultaneous husbands.

questions.question: 'Eravalla, Kadar, Muduvar ' are languages spoken by the tribes primarily in the state of ______.

__
 
• **'Eravalla, Kadar, Muduvar '** are languages spoken by the tribes primarily in the state of **Tamil Nadu.__**
 
• Dravidian languages, a family of around **70 languages** mainly spoken in South Asia.
 
• The Dravidian languages are split into groups in the South, South-Middle Central, and North; these groups are further split into 24 subgroups.
 
• The Constitution of India acknowledges the four major literary languages: Tamil Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada.
 
• They are also official languages, respectively, of the states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, and Karnataka (formerly Mysore).
 
• Tamil is the oldest of the four literary languages in the Dravidian family, with examples dating to the early Common Period.
 
• **Tolkappiyam (1st-4th century CE; "Ancient Literature"),** the first known work in the Tamil language, is a treatise on grammar and poetics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Until around the** 9th century CE**, Malayalam was the west coast dialect of Tamil. Geographically isolated by the steep Western Ghats from the main speech group, the dialect gradually evolved into a distinct language.
 
• Kannada is the official language in the state of Karnataka.
 
• The inscriptions in Kannada date from the **5th century CE, while Kavirajamarga ('The Royal Road of Poets'), the first literary work, is a ninth-century treatise on poetics.**
 
• Telugu is spoken by the greatest population among the Dravidian languages.
 
• It is the third most frequently spoken of all Indian languages, after Hindi and Bengali.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a viral disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Leprosy.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A chronic infectious disease, leprosy is caused by the bacteria, Mycobacterium leprae.**
 
• This condition mainly affects the skin causing pale sores, bumps and lumps on the skin.
 
• It also affects the peripheral nerves, eyes, and the mucosal linings of the respiratory system.
 
• Leprosy is a contagious disease that causes disfiguring skin sores and nerve damage in the arms, legs, and other regions of the body.
 
• It is caused by Mycobacterium leprae, a slow-growing pathogen (M. leprae).
 
• It is also known as Hansen's disease, after the man who discovered M. leprae in 1873. Leprosy is diagnosed based on the number and type of skin lesions you have.
 
• **The type of leprosy determines the symptoms and treatment options. Mycobacterium leprae is a bacterium that causes leprosy, often known as "Hansen's disease," **a chronic infectious disease that affects the skin, eyes, nose, and muscles and damages peripheral nerves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Measles:**

 
 
• It is caused by a virus named as** Rubeola virus.**
 
• It is airborne diseases that occur especially in children.
 
• **Symptoms:** Fever, Vomiting, Rashes on the skin.
 
• **Prevention:**
 
 
• Complete Rest.
 
• Drinking boiled, filtered water.
 
• Good light intake.
 
• Inoculation of gamma globulin.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Smallpox:**
 
 
• The smallpox vaccine was discovered by **Edward Jenner.**
 
• It was an infectious disease caused by one of two forms of the virus, Variola major and Variola minor.
 
• In** October 1977,** the last naturally occurring case was diagnosed, and in **1980, the World Health Organization (WHO) approved global eradication.**
 
• The Smallpox vaccine was the world's first vaccine.
 
 
 
• **Rabies:**
 
 
• It is caused by the **rabies virus.**
 
• The virus is spread through the saliva of infected animals.

questions.question: According to 'World Language Database Ethnologue-2019', brought out in February 2020, which Indian language is the third most spoken language of the world in 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Hindi.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **'World Language Database Ethnologue-2019'**, brought out in February 2020, Hindi language is the third most spoken language of the world in 2019.
 
• **Hindi is the third most spoken language in the world with 615 million speakers all over the world**.
 
• English is at the top with 1,132 million speakers followed by Mandarin with 1,117 million speakers.
 
• **On February 18, 2020**, the Ethnologue published its yearly database on living languages of the world.
 
• It covered more than** 7,111 living languages**.
 
• It also published data on languages that were gone out of usage in recent history and that included around **348 languages**.
 
• It also said that Bangla is the 7th most spoken language in the world with **228 million native speakers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken chiefly in India.**
 
• Hindi has been described as a standardized and Sanskritised register of the Hindustani language, which itself is based primarily on the Khariboli dialect of Delhi and neighbouring areas of Northern India.
 
• Hindi, written in the Devanagari script, is one of the two official languages of the Government of India, along with the English language.
 
• It is an official language in** 9 States and 3 Union Territories** and an additional official language in 3 other States.
 
• Hindi is also one of the** 22 scheduled languages of the Republic of India.**

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Kirana Gharana of classical music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Abdul Karim Khan.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abdul Karim Khan was the founder of the Kirana Gharana of classical music**.
 
• Kirana Gharana is one of the most prominent Indian classical khayal gharanas and is associated mostly with the perfect intonation of notes.
 
• The gharana's style was further evolved and was established as one of the important styles in modern Indian classical music in the late 19th /early 20th centuries by the musicians **Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan.**
 
• The name of this school of music comes from Kirana or Kairana, a town and tehsil of **Shamli District in Uttar Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gharana is a system in which people organize socially that links musicians and dancers.**
 
• It is an apprenticeship or lineage, for the adherence to a particular musical style.
 
• The word Gharana originates from the Urdu/Hindi word** 'Ghar", which means 'house' or Family.**
 
• A Gharana also indicates a comprehensive musicological ideology and differentiates one school from another.
 
• Some of the Gharanas well known for singing Hindustani classical music are Agra, Gwalior, Indore, Jaipur, Kirana, and Patiala.

questions.question: Which of the following schools in Shillong is the first Khelo India Sports school in NorthEast India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Assam Rifles Public School.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assam Rifles Public School is the first Sports School to be launched under the Khelo India Scheme in the North-East.**
 
• **Kiren Rijiju, Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports inaugurated the Assam Rifles Public School (ARPS) as a Khelo India Sports School in Shillong.**
 
• Currently, 9 Sports Schools have been approved across the country, with 5 of them being run by the military and paramilitary services.
 
• The government will now cover the costs of lodging, boarding, schooling, competition exposure, insurance & medical, sports training & support, salaries of coaches & support personnel, sports equipment, and more for the school's Talented Sports Students.
 
• **A Khelo India Sports School's goal is to connect sports and education, thereby developing sports in the country and improving players' whole profile and viewpoint**.
 
• This will also aid in the identification and development of talent in the North-East, rural, and tribal areas.
 
• Lt. Gen. Sukhdeep Sangwan, Director-General, Assam Rifles, was also praised by the Union Minister for his efforts in bringing various good reforms to the school over the years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In 2018**, Khelo India was launched.
 
• Its goal is to improve the country's sports culture.
 
• The** Rajiv Gandhi Khel Abhiyan, the National Sports Talent Search System, and the Urban Sports Infrastructure Scheme were merged to form Khelo India.**
 
• **"Sports for all" and "sports for excellence" are promoted in the programme.**

questions.question: With which of the following literary magazines was poet and writer Amrita Pritam associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Nagmani.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Amrita is considered a path-breaking woman, who rose to fame with her literary works like Pinjar, Suneray, and Nagmani.**
 
• **Amrita Pritam:**
 
 
• A renowned poetess, Amrita was born on** 31 August 1919 in Gujranwala, Punjab of British India, which now fall in Pakistan.**
 
• **She was the winner of the 17th Jnanpith Award.**
 
• Google doodle honoured Punjabi poetess Amrita Pritam with a doodle, marking her** 100th birthday.**
 
• She is considered to be the first poetess of the Punjabi language and is equally loved in both India and Pakistan.
 
• In her career of** 6 decades, she has written around 100 books**, including her famous autobiography** "Rasidi Ticket":**
 
 
• This book is an album of postage stamps.
 
• With each stamp, a new story unfolds on its postcard.
 
• The story doesn't have a closure which compels the reader to read the next chapter.
 
• In this book, she has written about her various phases of life.
 
 
 
• As a novelist her most important work was** Pinjar in 1950** whose background was the violence that happened against women and this novel made its way to an** award-winning film called Pinjar in 2003.**
 
• She was awarded** Padma Shri in 1969 **and** Padma Vibhushan and Sahitya Academy Award in 2004.**
